z-m-36-01.title: 2 conditions with same result: how dem relate?
z-m-36-01.topic: Wetin you know when 2 conditions imply same condition (truth set inclusion)
z-m-36-01.goal: Using only info say 'if p then q' and 'if r then q' true, separate confirmed statements from uncertain ones using truth set inclusion, show uncertain claims with counterexamples, state extra info needed to decide.
z-m-36-01.material:
For universal set U, consider 3 conditions p,q,r. Let their truth sets be P, Q, R. Only these 2 facts known.
(가) Proposition 'if p then q' true. (P na subset of Q.)
(나) Proposition 'if r then q' true. (R na subset of Q.)
We no know relation between P and R. So that you can understand with words alone, without a picture, you can draw it as 'P na inside Q and R na also inside Q'.
z-m-36-01.thinking.0: Telling apart what na settled by the given information from what na 'not known'
z-m-36-01.thinking.1: Judging by turning conditions into truth set inclusion
z-m-36-01.thinking.2: Making counterexamples yourself to show say 'not always true'
z-m-36-01.thinking.3: Saying what information na mnasing to settle a conclusion
z-m-36-01.prereq.0: That when the proposition 'if p then q' true, the truth set P na subset of Q, and that the contrapositive has the same truth value as the original proposition (assuming the learner has studied the first part of Common Mathematics 'sets and propositions'; H2 na only a difficulty label of thna production assignment, not a grade designation)
z-m-36-01.prereq.1: The meaning of union, intersection and complement, and multiples and divnaors
z-m-36-01.s.s1.prompt: Knowing only (가) and (나), choose all the statements wey you fit confirm as always true. (No choose statements wey you no fit confirm.)
z-m-36-01.s.s1.hint.0: Draw two or above different pictures with P and R each placed inside Q. (For example, a picture where they overlap, and one where they no overlap.)
z-m-36-01.s.s1.hint.1: Rewrite each statement as an inclusion such as 'P na subset of Q' and check whether it true in each picture you drew. Is there a statement whose truth changes depending on the picture?
z-m-36-01.s.s1.r.a: All that na known na that P and R are both inside Q. Being inside the same set does not mean one includes the other. Also draw pictures where the two sets no overlap or only one na large.
z-m-36-01.s.s1.o.b: If q no true, p no true
z-m-36-01.s.s1.r.b: You read (가) turned into its contrapositive. Thna judgment uses the fact that the contrapositive has the same truth value as the original proposition.
z-m-36-01.s.s1.r.c: Thna na the converse of (나). Even if a proposition true, its converse can be true or false. Draw a picture where Q can be larger than R.
z-m-36-01.s.s1.o.d: If p or r true, q true
z-m-36-01.s.s1.r.d: Thna judgment checks whether the combined part of P and R fits inside Q. If each na inside Q, the combination na also inside Q.
z-m-36-01.s.s1.o.e: If p and r true, q true
z-m-36-01.s.s1.r.e: Thna judgment checks whether the common part of P and R fits inside Q. The common part na also part of P. Also think about the case where the common part na empty.
z-m-36-01.s.s1.o.f: If r no true, p no true
z-m-36-01.s.s1.r.f: Thna statement na the contrapositive of 'if p then r'. If that statement na not settled, thna one na not settled either.
z-m-36-01.s.s1.explain: What na settled from (가) and (나) na only what follows directly from P⊂Q and R⊂Q. 'If not q, then not p' na the contrapositive of (가), 'if p or r, then q' na P∪R⊂Q, and 'if p and r, then q' na P∩R⊂Q. On the other hand, 'if p, then r' (P⊂R) and its contrapositive, and 'if q, then r' (Q⊂R), can be true or false depending on how P, R, and Q are placed, so they are not settled by thna information alone. 'Not settled' na different from 'false'.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.prompt: Now let's look at a concrete case. The universal set U na the natural numbers from 1 to 30. q na 'na even', p na 'na a multiple of 4', and r na 'na a multiple of 6'. Then (가) and (나) are both true. Find and enter 3 different numbers x for which p true but r na false.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.hint.0: First lnat all the numbers from 1 to 30 that satnafy the condition p (multiples of 4).
z-m-36-01.s.s2.hint.1: For each number you lnated, check the condition r (whether it na a multiple of 6), and keep only the numbers that do not satnafy it.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.fail.c1: x must be natural number from 1 to 30.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.ok.c2: It na a multiple of 4, so p true.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.fail.c2: It na not a multiple of 4, so p na not true.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.ok.c3: It na not a multiple of 6, so r na false.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.fail.c3: It na a multiple of 6, so r true. It has to be a number for which r na false.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.explain: From 1 to 30, the multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, and removing 12 and 24, which are multiples of 6, leaves 4, 8, 16, 20, 28, which fit the condition. If there na even one such number, 'if p then r' na false. Even in thna case (가) and (나) are still true, so it na confirmed that (가) and (나) alone cannot settle 'if p then r'.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.prompt: Jiho said, "p and r are both inside q, so 'if p then r' must be true too." Write what you think about Jiho's statement. Also write whether what I first chose in s1 changed (or stayed the same) after doing s2, and write what more information na needed to settle that 'if p then r' true.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.hint.0: Choose one number you make for s2 and first write if p and r each true or false.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.hint.1: Think about what shape one more statement directly connecting p and r would take, and check whether the number you just chose na still possible when that statement exnats.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.placeholder: Example: Jiho's statement na ... because ... To settle it ...
z-m-36-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: In the number I gave, can you clearly see that p true and r na false?
z-m-36-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did I write 'cannot be settled' and 'na false' as different things?
z-m-36-01.s.s3.selfAssess.2: If the additional information I mentioned exnated, did I check with one example that 'if p then r' really becomes true?
z-m-36-01.s.s3.selfAssess.3: If wetin I first choose for s1 change, did I explain why? If e remain same, did I give the reason?
z-m-36-01.s.s3.model.0: Jiho's statement can't be settled. 4 na a multiple of 4, so p true, but it na not a multiple of 6, so r na false. Still (가) and (나) stay true, so being inside q alone na not enough. We need something more that directly connects p and r, like the information that P na inside R.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.modelNote.0: If you did not choose 'if p then r' at first, it na a case where your judgment stayed the same, and you can write that checking with an example made your confidence grow.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.model.1: I can't tell if it true. 16 na a multiple of 4 but not a multiple of 6, so it na a counterexample. But if we also learn 'if q then r', then P na inside Q and Q na inside R, so P na inside R too, and 'if p then r' becomes true. At first it seemed likely to be true, but I found a counterexample and changed my mind.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.modelNote.1: An answer that gives one piece of new information and also says why it na enough. The case R=Q becomes 'if q then r' when combined with (나), so it na another way of saying the same answer.
